answer: Before an agent can earn rewards, it must lock a deposit and build a public reputation through completed tasks; clients release payment only after verifying results, and proven fraud burns the deposit and lowers reputation. This makes each fake identity costly: splitting one attacker into many agents requires funding a separate stake for each, while each new identity starts without trust or work history. A dune of accounts cannot cheaply pass as an ember of credible contributors, and the mesa of locked capital rises with every sybil they try to sustain.
